subtopic: FP8 mul + FP32 accum on Hopper
learningObjective: Explain FP8 matmul semantics on Hopper Tensor Cores including accumulator dtype and scaling requirements.
stem: On Hopper Tensor Cores, FP8 (E4M3/E5M2) matmul is a common training precision. Which of the following statements about the FP8 GEMM numerical pipeline are TRUE? (Select all that apply.)
profileData:
Hopper H100 Tensor Core peak throughput (dense, per NVIDIA whitepaper):
  BF16 / FP16      : ~ 989 TFLOPS
  FP8 (E4M3, E5M2) : ~1979 TFLOPS  (~ 2×)
  Accumulator dtype in FP8 QMMA/WGMMA: FP32.
  Transformer Engine 'DelayedScaling' recipe: per-tensor scale factors updated with a lag over recent statistics.

options.text: FP8 Tensor Core matmuls use an FP32 accumulator; the per-tile accumulator is FP32 regardless of whether inputs are E4M3 or E5M2. This mitigates the very limited dynamic range of FP8 for the sum of products.

Because FP8's dynamic range is small, production FP8 pipelines apply per-tensor (or per-block) scale factors that keep the values within FP8's representable range; NVIDIA's Transformer Engine automates this via its `DelayedScaling` recipe.
FP8 GEMM on H100 has approximately 2× the peak throughput of BF16 GEMM on the same hardware, but only when memory bandwidth is not the bottleneck.
The FP8 accumulator is itself FP8; the small dynamic range is deliberately preserved to force early saturation, which acts as an implicit regularizer.
FP8 GEMM on H100 delivers its compute advantage automatically for any FP16 model; no code or precision-management change is required.

explanation: A: FP8 Tensor Core matmuls accumulate in FP32 (parallel to FP16/BF16 → FP32 accumulation). B: FP8's dynamic range is small (E4M3 ~±448, E5M2 ~±57344); production stacks apply scaling to keep values in range, with Transformer Engine automating it. C: H100 FP8 peak is roughly 2× BF16 peak (per NVIDIA specs), but the ratio only holds for compute-bound kernels. D is false: no framework uses FP8 accumulators for main compute; the small range makes this impractical. E is false: FP8 requires opt-in and scale management; frameworks do not silently convert FP16 to FP8.

optionExplanations.A: Correct: FP32 accumulator is standard for FP8 Tensor Cores.
optionExplanations.C: Correct: peak-throughput advantage in compute-bound regimes.
optionExplanations.D: Wrong: no FP8 accumulator in production paths.
optionExplanations.E: Wrong: FP8 requires explicit opt-in and scale management.

assumptions: The target GPU is Hopper (sm_90) with FP8 Tensor Core support.
The workload uses NVIDIA's Transformer Engine or equivalent FP8 pipeline.
nonImplications: Does not imply FP8 always matches BF16 accuracy — small residual differences are typical, and workload-dependent.
Does not imply the 2× peak is always realized — memory-bandwidth-bound kernels see much less benefit.

distractorRationales.D: Invents an FP8 accumulator that no production path uses.

sourceRefs.locator: H100 FP8 Tensor Core specification; QMMA / WGMMA
